There is a growing crop of genre movies that perform exceptionally well on PVOD and streaming after they get a robust marketing push thanks to a theatrical run. These movies typically have a standard benchmark of around $15 million at the box office, which appears to be enough to recoup marketing costs and generate publicity for when they hit the home-video market. Some shining examples of the last few months are the World War II movies Pressure and Nuremberg, and the Jason Statham vehicles Mutiny and Shelter. Now, a new action movie is on track to join their ranks after overtaking one of the year’s most high-profile underperformers.

The new movie stars Alan Ritchson in the lead role, alongside Owen Wilson. It was released a couple of weeks ago by Angel Studios, a company that specializes in faith-based content, but has been expanding its scope with genre movies that happen to have religious undertones. Ritchson, of course, has cultivated a large following on streaming thanks to Prime Video’s blockbuster series Reacher, which recently concluded its fourth season. Ritchson’s new movie was given a theatrical release that coincided with the Reacher Season 4 finale, and the launch of the spin-off series Neagley.

The first few seconds tell you everything about who belongs beside you.

ASomeone who already has three contingency plans running and is calmly working through all of them.

CSomeone who keeps their nerve and their sense of humour when everything is falling apart.
DSomeone who knows the history of wherever we are and what we're walking into.
ESomeone with the right contact, the right cover identity, and the right exit already arranged.

You have to get somewhere dangerous, fast. How do you travel?
How you get there is half the mission.

AOn foot through terrain no one else would attempt — I move where vehicles can't follow.
BOn a motorcycle, a cargo plane, or anything else that gets me there before I think too hard about it.
CIn something that belongs to someone else — borrowed, stolen, or improvised under fire.
DFirst class, with a cover identity and a gadget that does something I won't explain until it's needed.
EBy whatever means are available — I've driven, flown, and once arrived by camel. The destination matters, not the method.

You're pinned down and outnumbered. What does your ideal partner do?
This is when you find out what someone is really made of.

ADisappears into the environment, flanks them silently, and ends it before I've reloaded.
BCracks a one-liner, grabs a fire extinguisher or a chair, and improvises something that somehow works.
CProduces a gadget specifically designed for this exact scenario and uses it with infuriating precision.
